title: Completed affine sections of a power-torsion quasi-coherent sheaf
statement: Let $Y$ be a Noetherian scheme, $J$ an ideal sheaf, $U$ an affine open, $B=\Gamma(Y,U)$, $R=\widehat{B}_{J(U)}$ the completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $g:\operatorname{Spec} R\to Y$ the completion ring map followed by the affine chart inclusion. Let $A$ evaluate module sheaves on $U$, and let $P$ be tensor pullback along $g$ followed by global Spec sections and restriction of scalars along $B\to R$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. There exists a natural transformation $c:A\to P$ such that, for every quasi-coherent module sheaf $M$ [pqf-def-coherent] and every $n\in\mathbb N$ with $J(U)^{n+1}\Gamma(U,M)=0$, $c_M$ is an isomorphism of $B$-modules. This concerns individual sheaves and includes no formal system or diagram transitions.

source.place: Completed base-change paragraph; Tags 05GG (completion quotient) and 01I9 (affine pullback).

proof.text: Construct the comparison from the tensor-pullback adjunction unit on U followed by restriction to top on Spec R. The completion morphism factors through the affine chart, so the inverse image of U is top. The chart structure-ring map on global sections is the algebra map B to R followed by the inverse Spec global-section isomorphism; this proves B-linearity. Unit naturality and restriction naturality prove the comparison natural.

Apply the affine pullback sections comparison to U and the top affine open of Spec R. Transport the ring-section factor along the Spec global-section linear equivalence and swap tensor factors. This gives a B-linear equivalence from R tensor_B M(U) to the comparison target, carrying 1 tensor x to the comparison component on x.

Since B is Noetherian the completion ideal I is finitely generated. Use the completion evaluation, its surjectivity and its kernel I^n R to identify R/I^n R with B/I^n. The tensor/quotient equivalences in Mathlib then give M/I^n M equivalent to (R tensor_B M)/I^n(R tensor_B M), with x mapping to 1 tensor x. If I^n M is zero, tensor induction shows I^n(R tensor_B M) is zero too. The two quotient maps are injective and surjective, so the displayed equivalence proves the tensor unit bijective. Compose with the affine-section equivalence and use the concrete ModuleCat bijectivity criterion to obtain IsIso.

lean.statement:
theorem completedAffineSections_powerTorsion
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian Y] (J : Y.IdealSheafData) (U : Y.affineOpens) :
    let B := Γ(Y, U.1)
    let R := AdicCompletion (J.ideal U) B
    let S := Spec (CommRingCat.of R)
    let g : S ⟶ Y := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B R)) ≫
      U.2.isoSpec.inv ≫ U.1.ι
    let T := Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback g
    let E := moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := CommRingCat.of R)
    let L := ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap B R)
    ∃ c : SheafOfModules.evaluation Y.ringCatSheaf (op U.1) ⟶ T ⋙ E ⋙ L,
      ∀ (M : Y.Modules) (_ : M.IsQuasicoherent) (n : ℕ),
        J.ideal U ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule B Γ(M, U.1)) = ⊥ →
          IsIso (c.app M)
